hyperedges.label: What Makes an Editor Viewport Possible

nodes.label: CI Cross-Platform Build Matrix
nodes.rationale: Builds Windows, macOS and Linux with a vcpkg binary cache keyed on vcpkg.json.

nodes.label: Desktop-First Platform Targets
nodes.rationale: Windows, macOS and Linux now; Android and iOS once the render backend supports them.

nodes.label: B1: Fixed-Function OpenGL
nodes.rationale: Renderer.cpp draws with glPushMatrix/glVertexPointer/glEnableClientState - the GL 1.x pipeline. No shaders means no 3D lighting; ImGui needs a 3.0+ context, so no editor either. Both goals are downstream of this.

nodes.label: D2: One RHI, Two Renderers
nodes.rationale: A thin RHI over Buffer/Texture/Shader/Framebuffer with an OpenGL backend, with Renderer2D (batched quads) and Renderer3D (forward PBR-lite) above it. Both draw into a Framebuffer so the editor can show the game inside an ImGui panel.

nodes.label: OpenGL 3.3 Core Baseline
nodes.rationale: Revised down from 4.5. macOS caps at 4.1 and deprecated GL in 2018, so DSA and compute shaders are unavailable there. 3.3 is the highest version Windows, macOS and Linux share, and maps onto GLES 3.0 for Android. iOS needs Metal regardless.

nodes.label: D6: Dear ImGui Editor
nodes.rationale: Docking branch plus ImGuizmo. Immediate mode means no state-sync bugs between UI and scene - the panel re-reads the entity every frame.

nodes.label: glad Regenerated for 3.3 Core
nodes.rationale: The vendored loader only reached GL 2.1 on the compatibility profile, so it still exported glPushMatrix and friends. Regenerating for 3.3 core removed them, which is what surfaced every remaining fixed-function call site at compile time.

nodes.label: Offscreen Scene Target
nodes.rationale: Every frame renders into a Framebuffer and is blitted to the window. The runtime pays one blit; in exchange the editor can hand the same colour attachment to a viewport panel without the renderer knowing it is being embedded.

nodes.label: Switch-Indexed Sampler Array
nodes.rationale: GLSL 330 requires a constant expression to index a sampler array, so the fragment shader dispatches through a switch rather than subscripting with the varying.

nodes.label: White Texture in Slot 0
nodes.rationale: A 1x1 opaque white texture occupies slot 0 so untextured quads multiply against it and share the textured path. Avoids a second shader and a per-quad branch.

nodes.label: Layout-Driven Vertex Attributes
nodes.rationale: BufferLayout carries element types, offsets and stride, and VertexArray wires the attribute pointers from it. Integer attributes route through glVertexAttribIPointer and matrices consume one slot per column.

nodes.label: RHI Abstraction Layer
nodes.rationale: Shader, Buffer, VertexArray and Framebuffer wrap the GL objects behind types the renderer talks to. One backend today, but it is the seam Vulkan and Metal slot into - and it forces render state out of the old global Renderer statics.

nodes.label: B4: Static God Classes
nodes.rationale: Camera, Renderer, Input, GameObjectCollection, SceneStateMachine, Graphics and TextureAllocator are entirely static. An editor needs two live cameras, two viewports and world teardown on Play/Stop - global state forbids all three.

nodes.label: D4: Camera as Component
nodes.rationale: CameraComponent plus a separate EditorCamera. The editor camera must fly around while the game camera sits untouched - what the current static Camera cannot express.

nodes.label: CI Naming Gate
nodes.rationale: Greps the tree for coursework identifiers and fails the build if any return. Excludes docs/ (which documents the cleanup) and itself (it defines the pattern).

nodes.label: B12: Coursework Naming
nodes.rationale: xbgt3124_t03 project files, 0130645_Doxyfile and generated docs carried student-ID and course-code identifiers throughout.

nodes.label: Strangler-Fig Migration
nodes.rationale: Files move with git mv so history follows them, CMake builds the existing code first, and subsystems modernise one at a time. The tree stays buildable at every commit.

nodes.label: B6: 2D-Only Transform
nodes.rationale: Transform stores vec2 position, float rotation, vec2 scale, and Camera only builds glm::ortho. 3D is not expressible.

nodes.label: D3: Unified 3D Transform
nodes.rationale: One vec3 TransformComponent with vec2 overloads. Two transform types would bifurcate the renderer, physics, serializer and gizmos; 48 bytes vs 20 is not a real cost next to two parallel hierarchies.

nodes.label: D10: Native C++ Now, Lua Later
nodes.rationale: NativeScriptComponent covers Phases 0-4; Lua via sol2 arrives in Phase 5. C# via Mono is a much larger project and is not recommended at this stage.
nodes.norm_label: d10: native c++ now, lua later

nodes.label: B10: Busy-Wait Frame Limiter
nodes.rationale: Time::processTime spun on glfwGetTime(), burning a full CPU core to cap the framerate.

nodes.label: B11: Member Initialisation Order Bug
nodes.rationale: Application declared window before windowData but initialised them in the opposite order. C++ follows declaration order, so window was built from uninitialised data.

nodes.label: B7: No Serialization
nodes.rationale: Nothing writes a scene to disk or reads one back. An editor that cannot save is a toy.

nodes.label: B8: dynamic_cast Component Lookup
nodes.rationale: getComponent<T>() walks every component doing an RTTI cast per element - O(n) per lookup, per frame.

nodes.label: Batched Quad Renderer
nodes.rationale: Quads accumulate into one dynamic VBO with a 16-slot texture array, so a scene of sprites costs one draw call per batch rather than one per sprite. Batches flush on quad limit, texture-slot exhaustion, or end of scene.

nodes.label: D1: EnTT Entity Model
nodes.rationale: Scene owns an entt::registry; Entity is an opaque handle. Chosen for O(1) typed access, contiguous storage and iterate-by-component - the one mechanism the renderer, serializer and inspector all need. Cost: GameObject, GameObjectCollection and BaseComponent get rewritten.

nodes.label: D5: YAML Scene Serialization
nodes.rationale: Scenes as .scrapscene via yaml-cpp. Chosen over JSON because scene files get committed and merged, and YAML diffs readably.

nodes.label: scrap_warnings Interface Target
nodes.rationale: Shared warning flags for every first-party target. Deliberately not -Werror yet - the 0.7 sources still trip several and Phase 1 clears them.

nodes.label: ScrapEngine CMake Project
nodes.rationale: Root project: C++17, single output tree, shared scrap_warnings interface target. Picks up the vcpkg toolchain from VCPKG_ROOT before project().

nodes.label: ScrapEngine Library Target
nodes.rationale: Static library aliased Scrap::Engine. Only include and src go on the include path.

nodes.label: Sandbox Executable Target
nodes.rationale: The demo game, linking Scrap::Engine. Assets stage as a sibling of bin/ because the sources load them as ../assets/...

nodes.label: glad Target
nodes.rationale: Vendored GL loader, checked in rather than fetched because it is generated per GL profile.

nodes.label: stb Target
nodes.rationale: Header-only stb_image, exposed as an INTERFACE target.

nodes.label: Shared AudioDevice
nodes.rationale: Every AudioSource previously constructed an entire irrKlang sound engine of its own. One process-wide device now starts lazily and all sources mix into it.

nodes.label: B13: MSBuild Only, No CI
nodes.rationale: No CMake meant no portability, no continuous integration, and no way to express a multi-target build.

nodes.label: B2: Absolute Include Paths
nodes.rationale: The vcxproj hardcoded include paths into ToGoGameEngine_0.4, a directory not in the repository.

nodes.label: B3: Missing Link Libraries
nodes.rationale: freetype.lib, irrKlang.lib and glfw3.lib were linked but deps/lib held only irrKlang.exp; .gitignore excluded *.lib so they were never committed.

nodes.label: B5: Game Compiled Into Engine
nodes.rationale: Game scenes and main.cpp shared a target with Renderer, so there was no engine library for an editor or shipped game to link against.

nodes.label: D7: CMake and vcpkg
nodes.rationale: CMake still generates a VS solution, but the absolute-path and single-target problems disappear. A vcpkg manifest fixes the missing-binaries problem by not vendoring binaries at all.

nodes.label: D8: miniaudio over irrKlang
nodes.rationale: irrKlang is closed-source, its binaries were absent from the repo, and it is paid for commercial use with no mobile story. miniaudio is a single public-domain header with 3D spatial audio built in. Pulled forward from Phase 5 because nothing could link without it.

nodes.label: Engine Included a Game Scene
nodes.rationale: Application.cpp included MainMenuScene.h - the engine directly depending on game code, the rawest form of B5.

nodes.label: Module-Qualified Includes
nodes.rationale: Only engine/src is on the include path; engine headers are included as "renderer/Camera.h". A down payment on the Phase 1 <Scrap/...> public API.

nodes.label: Time.h Shadowed the CRT time.h
nodes.rationale: With engine/src/core on the include path, Windows case-insensitive filesystem resolved <ctime>'s internal #include <time.h> to the engine header, breaking every TU that touched <ctime>. Forced module-qualified includes early.
